## Claim protocol — read before you start

This issue is claimable by an opencode agent (key 1 or key 2) or a zcode agent.
Before touching any repository file, post a comment on this issue:

```
CLAIM <agent-id> <provider> <UTC ISO-8601 timestamp>
```

Then re-read the comments and confirm your claim is the first valid one. If it
is not, comment `RELEASE <agent-id> conflict` and pick another issue. One agent
holds one issue at a time in this repository. A claim held more than 24 h with
no `DONE` comment becomes stale; the first `STALE` comment releases it. Finish
with `DONE <commit-sha> <one-line result>`.

No agent may work an issue another agent has claimed, on any provider or in
any harness. Commits made without a winning claim are protocol violations.

## Discipline (all issues)

- RULE 0: search the web and GitHub code FIRST, record exact query strings and
  dates in the deliverable. Prior art found means do not rebuild; find the delta.
- RULE 1: fix any stale count, dangling reference or broken link you notice in
  the same session, respecting file walls; list before/after in your report.
- Facts-not-blobs: never commit a proprietary payload. Hashes, sizes, offsets,
  counts and <=16-byte hex samples only.
- Standard library Python only; run scripts with `python3 -I`.
- No comments or docstrings in Python code.
- Every success claim verified by command output before it is written.
- Honest negatives are deliverables.
- Do not push. Commit locally only; the lead pushes.

## Task
Verify that the committed type, build variant and note for **6.1_2018** are correct against repository evidence.

Current: type=`phone`, build_variant=`mobile`, note=``.

## Deliverable
A comment on this issue with CONFIRM or a proposed change plus the exact file:line evidence. If a change is needed, propose it as a one-line diff; do not edit `site/data/device-types.csv` without a winning claim.

## Acceptance
- Hardware type, not firmware image, is what `type` means.
- Foldables are phones; `_Tablet` boards are the type of their `_TV` sibling.
- ATV set is exactly the 8 named devices.
title: Audit device classification for 6.1_2018

## Claim protocol — read before you start

This issue is claimable by an opencode agent (key 1 or key 2) or a zcode agent.
Before touching any repository file, post a comment on this issue:

```
CLAIM <agent-id> <provider> <UTC ISO-8601 timestamp>
```

Then re-read the comments and confirm your claim is the first valid one. If it
is not, comment `RELEASE <agent-id> conflict` and pick another issue. One agent
holds one issue at a time in this repository. A claim held more than 24 h with
no `DONE` comment becomes stale; the first `STALE` comment releases it. Finish
with `DONE <commit-sha> <one-line result>`.

No agent may work an issue another agent has claimed, on any provider or in
any harness. Commits made without a winning claim are protocol violations.

## Discipline (all issues)

- RULE 0: search the web and GitHub code FIRST, record exact query strings and
  dates in the deliverable. Prior art found means do not rebuild; find the delta.
- RULE 1: fix any stale count, dangling reference or broken link you notice in
  the same session, respecting file walls; list before/after in your report.
- Facts-not-blobs: never commit a proprietary payload. Hashes, sizes, offsets,
  counts and <=16-byte hex samples only.
- Standard library Python only; run scripts with `python3 -I`.
- No comments or docstrings in Python code.
- Every success claim verified by command output before it is written.
- Honest negatives are deliverables.
- Do not push. Commit locally only; the lead pushes.

This issue is claimable by an opencode agent (key 1 or key 2) or a zcode agent.
Before touching any repository file, post a comment on this issue:

```
CLAIM <agent-id> <provider> <UTC ISO-8601 timestamp>
```

Then re-read the comments and confirm your claim is the first valid one. If it
is not, comment `RELEASE <agent-id> conflict` and pick another issue. One agent
holds one issue at a time in this repository. A claim held more than 24 h with
no `DONE` comment becomes stale; the first `STALE` comment releases it. Finish
with `DONE <commit-sha> <one-line result>`.

No agent may work an issue another agent has claimed, on any provider or in
any harness. Commits made without a winning claim are protocol violations.

## Discipline (all issues)

- RULE 0: search the web and GitHub code FIRST, record exact query strings and
  dates in the deliverable. Prior art found means do not rebuild; find the delta.
- RULE 1: fix any stale count, dangling reference or broken link you notice in
  the same session, respecting file walls; list before/after in your report.
- Facts-not-blobs: never commit a proprietary payload. Hashes, sizes, offsets,
  counts and <=16-byte hex samples only.
- Standard library Python only; run scripts with `python3 -I`.
- No comments or docstrings in Python code.
- Every success claim verified by command output before it is written.
- Honest negatives are deliverables.
- Do not push. Commit locally only; the lead pushes.

This issue is claimable by an opencode agent (key 1 or key 2) or a zcode agent.
Before touching any repository file, post a comment on this issue:

```
CLAIM <agent-id> <provider> <UTC ISO-8601 timestamp>
```

Then re-read the comments and confirm your claim is the first valid one. If it
is not, comment `RELEASE <agent-id> conflict` and pick another issue. One agent
holds one issue at a time in this repository. A claim held more than 24 h with
no `DONE` comment becomes stale; the first `STALE` comment releases it. Finish
with `DONE <commit-sha> <one-line result>`.

No agent may work an issue another agent has claimed, on any provider or in
any harness. Commits made without a winning claim are protocol violations.

## Discipline (all issues)

- RULE 0: search the web and GitHub code FIRST, record exact query strings and
  dates in the deliverable. Prior art found means do not rebuild; find the delta.
- RULE 1: fix any stale count, dangling reference or broken link you notice in
  the same session, respecting file walls; list before/after in your report.
- Facts-not-blobs: never commit a proprietary payload. Hashes, sizes, offsets,
  counts and <=16-byte hex samples only.
- Standard library Python only; run scripts with `python3 -I`.
- No comments or docstrings in Python code.
- Every success claim verified by command output before it is written.
- Honest negatives are deliverables.
- Do not push. Commit locally only; the lead pushes.

This issue is claimable by an opencode agent (key 1 or key 2) or a zcode agent.
Before touching any repository file, post a comment on this issue:

```
CLAIM <agent-id> <provider> <UTC ISO-8601 timestamp>
```

Then re-read the comments and confirm your claim is the first valid one. If it
is not, comment `RELEASE <agent-id> conflict` and pick another issue. One agent
holds one issue at a time in this repository. A claim held more than 24 h with
no `DONE` comment becomes stale; the first `STALE` comment releases it. Finish
with `DONE <commit-sha> <one-line result>`.

No agent may work an issue another agent has claimed, on any provider or in
any harness. Commits made without a winning claim are protocol violations.

## Discipline (all issues)

- RULE 0: search the web and GitHub code FIRST, record exact query strings and
  dates in the deliverable. Prior art found means do not rebuild; find the delta.
- RULE 1: fix any stale count, dangling reference or broken link you notice in
  the same session, respecting file walls; list before/after in your report.
- Facts-not-blobs: never commit a proprietary payload. Hashes, sizes, offsets,
  counts and <=16-byte hex samples only.
- Standard library Python only; run scripts with `python3 -I`.
- No comments or docstrings in Python code.
- Every success claim verified by command output before it is written.
- Honest negatives are deliverables.
- Do not push. Commit locally only; the lead pushes.

## Task
The coverage matrix has no `other` rows for **Mi_11**. Verify whether that is a real structural absence or a census gap.

## Deliverable
One paragraph under `docs/devices/<vendor>/Mi_11/other.md` stating ABSENT with the evidence, or a corrected matrix row if the absence is false.

## Acceptance
- Structural absence (no partition) is distinguished from a census gap (partition exists, not walked).
- A negative result is reported as a finding, not omitted.
- RULE 0 prior-art search with exact queries and dates.
title: Verify other is absent for Mi_11 (honest negative)

This issue is claimable by an opencode agent (key 1 or key 2) or a zcode agent.
Before touching any repository file, post a comment on this issue:

```
CLAIM <agent-id> <provider> <UTC ISO-8601 timestamp>
```

Then re-read the comments and confirm your claim is the first valid one. If it
is not, comment `RELEASE <agent-id> conflict` and pick another issue. One agent
holds one issue at a time in this repository. A claim held more than 24 h with
no `DONE` comment becomes stale; the first `STALE` comment releases it. Finish
with `DONE <commit-sha> <one-line result>`.

No agent may work an issue another agent has claimed, on any provider or in
any harness. Commits made without a winning claim are protocol violations.

## Discipline (all issues)

- RULE 0: search the web and GitHub code FIRST, record exact query strings and
  dates in the deliverable. Prior art found means do not rebuild; find the delta.
- RULE 1: fix any stale count, dangling reference or broken link you notice in
  the same session, respecting file walls; list before/after in your report.
- Facts-not-blobs: never commit a proprietary payload. Hashes, sizes, offsets,
  counts and <=16-byte hex samples only.
- Standard library Python only; run scripts with `python3 -I`.
- No comments or docstrings in Python code.
- Every success claim verified by command output before it is written.
- Honest negatives are deliverables.
- Do not push. Commit locally only; the lead pushes.

## Task
The coverage matrix has no `modem` rows for **Nord_N20_5G**. Verify whether that is a real structural absence or a census gap.

## Deliverable
One paragraph under `docs/devices/<vendor>/Nord_N20_5G/modem.md` stating ABSENT with the evidence, or a corrected matrix row if the absence is false.

## Acceptance
- Structural absence (no partition) is distinguished from a census gap (partition exists, not walked).
- A negative result is reported as a finding, not omitted.
- RULE 0 prior-art search with exact queries and dates.
title: Verify modem is absent for Nord_N20_5G (honest negative)

This issue is claimable by an opencode agent (key 1 or key 2) or a zcode agent.
Before touching any repository file, post a comment on this issue:

```
CLAIM <agent-id> <provider> <UTC ISO-8601 timestamp>
```

Then re-read the comments and confirm your claim is the first valid one. If it
is not, comment `RELEASE <agent-id> conflict` and pick another issue. One agent
holds one issue at a time in this repository. A claim held more than 24 h with
no `DONE` comment becomes stale; the first `STALE` comment releases it. Finish
with `DONE <commit-sha> <one-line result>`.

No agent may work an issue another agent has claimed, on any provider or in
any harness. Commits made without a winning claim are protocol violations.

## Discipline (all issues)

- RULE 0: search the web and GitHub code FIRST, record exact query strings and
  dates in the deliverable. Prior art found means do not rebuild; find the delta.
- RULE 1: fix any stale count, dangling reference or broken link you notice in
  the same session, respecting file walls; list before/after in your report.
- Facts-not-blobs: never commit a proprietary payload. Hashes, sizes, offsets,
  counts and <=16-byte hex samples only.
- Standard library Python only; run scripts with `python3 -I`.
- No comments or docstrings in Python code.
- Every success claim verified by command output before it is written.
- Honest negatives are deliverables.
- Do not push. Commit locally only; the lead pushes.

## Task
The coverage matrix has no `other` rows for **Pixel_2**. Verify whether that is a real structural absence or a census gap.

## Deliverable
One paragraph under `docs/devices/<vendor>/Pixel_2/other.md` stating ABSENT with the evidence, or a corrected matrix row if the absence is false.

## Acceptance
- Structural absence (no partition) is distinguished from a census gap (partition exists, not walked).
- A negative result is reported as a finding, not omitted.
- RULE 0 prior-art search with exact queries and dates.
title: Verify other is absent for Pixel_2 (honest negative)

This issue is claimable by an opencode agent (key 1 or key 2) or a zcode agent.
Before touching any repository file, post a comment on this issue:

```
CLAIM <agent-id> <provider> <UTC ISO-8601 timestamp>
```

Then re-read the comments and confirm your claim is the first valid one. If it
is not, comment `RELEASE <agent-id> conflict` and pick another issue. One agent
holds one issue at a time in this repository. A claim held more than 24 h with
no `DONE` comment becomes stale; the first `STALE` comment releases it. Finish
with `DONE <commit-sha> <one-line result>`.

No agent may work an issue another agent has claimed, on any provider or in
any harness. Commits made without a winning claim are protocol violations.

## Discipline (all issues)

- RULE 0: search the web and GitHub code FIRST, record exact query strings and
  dates in the deliverable. Prior art found means do not rebuild; find the delta.
- RULE 1: fix any stale count, dangling reference or broken link you notice in
  the same session, respecting file walls; list before/after in your report.
- Facts-not-blobs: never commit a proprietary payload. Hashes, sizes, offsets,
  counts and <=16-byte hex samples only.
- Standard library Python only; run scripts with `python3 -I`.
- No comments or docstrings in Python code.
- Every success claim verified by command output before it is written.
- Honest negatives are deliverables.
- Do not push. Commit locally only; the lead pushes.

## Task
The coverage matrix has no `tz` rows for **Poco_12C**. Verify whether that is a real structural absence or a census gap.

## Deliverable
One paragraph under `docs/devices/<vendor>/Poco_12C/tz.md` stating ABSENT with the evidence, or a corrected matrix row if the absence is false.

## Acceptance
- Structural absence (no partition) is distinguished from a census gap (partition exists, not walked).
- A negative result is reported as a finding, not omitted.
- RULE 0 prior-art search with exact queries and dates.
title: Verify tz is absent for Poco_12C (honest negative)

This issue is claimable by an opencode agent (key 1 or key 2) or a zcode agent.
Before touching any repository file, post a comment on this issue:

```
CLAIM <agent-id> <provider> <UTC ISO-8601 timestamp>
```

Then re-read the comments and confirm your claim is the first valid one. If it
is not, comment `RELEASE <agent-id> conflict` and pick another issue. One agent
holds one issue at a time in this repository. A claim held more than 24 h with
no `DONE` comment becomes stale; the first `STALE` comment releases it. Finish
with `DONE <commit-sha> <one-line result>`.

No agent may work an issue another agent has claimed, on any provider or in
any harness. Commits made without a winning claim are protocol violations.

## Discipline (all issues)

- RULE 0: search the web and GitHub code FIRST, record exact query strings and
  dates in the deliverable. Prior art found means do not rebuild; find the delta.
- RULE 1: fix any stale count, dangling reference or broken link you notice in
  the same session, respecting file walls; list before/after in your report.
- Facts-not-blobs: never commit a proprietary payload. Hashes, sizes, offsets,
  counts and <=16-byte hex samples only.
- Standard library Python only; run scripts with `python3 -I`.
- No comments or docstrings in Python code.
- Every success claim verified by command output before it is written.
- Honest negatives are deliverables.
- Do not push. Commit locally only; the lead pushes.

## Task
The coverage matrix has no `gpu` rows for **V30**. Verify whether that is a real structural absence or a census gap.

## Deliverable
One paragraph under `docs/devices/<vendor>/V30/gpu.md` stating ABSENT with the evidence, or a corrected matrix row if the absence is false.

## Acceptance
- Structural absence (no partition) is distinguished from a census gap (partition exists, not walked).
- A negative result is reported as a finding, not omitted.
- RULE 0 prior-art search with exact queries and dates.
title: Verify gpu is absent for V30 (honest negative)

This issue is claimable by an opencode agent (key 1 or key 2) or a zcode agent.
Before touching any repository file, post a comment on this issue:

```
CLAIM <agent-id> <provider> <UTC ISO-8601 timestamp>
```

Then re-read the comments and confirm your claim is the first valid one. If it
is not, comment `RELEASE <agent-id> conflict` and pick another issue. One agent
holds one issue at a time in this repository. A claim held more than 24 h with
no `DONE` comment becomes stale; the first `STALE` comment releases it. Finish
with `DONE <commit-sha> <one-line result>`.

No agent may work an issue another agent has claimed, on any provider or in
any harness. Commits made without a winning claim are protocol violations.

## Discipline (all issues)

- RULE 0: search the web and GitHub code FIRST, record exact query strings and
  dates in the deliverable. Prior art found means do not rebuild; find the delta.
- RULE 1: fix any stale count, dangling reference or broken link you notice in
  the same session, respecting file walls; list before/after in your report.
- Facts-not-blobs: never commit a proprietary payload. Hashes, sizes, offsets,
  counts and <=16-byte hex samples only.
- Standard library Python only; run scripts with `python3 -I`.
- No comments or docstrings in Python code.
- Every success claim verified by command output before it is written.
- Honest negatives are deliverables.
- Do not push. Commit locally only; the lead pushes.

Cross-reference MTK interface claims against the AOSP kernel.

## Deliverable
An evidence-classed Markdown note or a verified code change, plus the exact commands and output that prove the result.

## Acceptance
- RULE 0 prior-art search with exact queries and dates.
- Honest negatives recorded where the evidence runs out.
- No proprietary payload committed.

title: Cross-reference MTK interface claims against the AOSP kernel

This issue is claimable by an opencode agent (key 1 or key 2) or a zcode agent.
Before touching any repository file, post a comment on this issue:

```
CLAIM <agent-id> <provider> <UTC ISO-8601 timestamp>
```

Then re-read the comments and confirm your claim is the first valid one. If it
is not, comment `RELEASE <agent-id> conflict` and pick another issue. One agent
holds one issue at a time in this repository. A claim held more than 24 h with
no `DONE` comment becomes stale; the first `STALE` comment releases it. Finish
with `DONE <commit-sha> <one-line result>`.

No agent may work an issue another agent has claimed, on any provider or in
any harness. Commits made without a winning claim are protocol violations.

## Discipline (all issues)

- RULE 0: search the web and GitHub code FIRST, record exact query strings and
  dates in the deliverable. Prior art found means do not rebuild; find the delta.
- RULE 1: fix any stale count, dangling reference or broken link you notice in
  the same session, respecting file walls; list before/after in your report.
- Facts-not-blobs: never commit a proprietary payload. Hashes, sizes, offsets,
  counts and <=16-byte hex samples only.
- Standard library Python only; run scripts with `python3 -I`.
- No comments or docstrings in Python code.
- Every success claim verified by command output before it is written.
- Honest negatives are deliverables.
- Do not push. Commit locally only; the lead pushes.

## Deliverable
The implementation plus its unittest tests, committed locally.

## Acceptance
- Tests pass under `python3 -I`.
- No third-party imports, no network calls.
- Output deterministic.
